Senior Music and Drama
Performing Arts is thriving at Beechwood. Building on the successful Senior School productions, more students are opting for Music and Drama at GCSE and A-Level.
Over one third of the school have private music lessons from one of our visiting teachers and many opt to study for their LAMDA (London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art) exams. Students in Year 7-9 have Drama and Music lessons timetabled each week.
Recent school productions have included Grease, We Will Rock You and High School Musical. The Autumn term heralds our Cultural Showcase where students in both the Performing and Creative Arts departments can display their skills and talents to a packed audience. Throughout the year, there is a series of Lunchtime recitals for students to perform in a more intimate setting.
Students have the opportunity to see live theatre productions and recent visits have included Grease in the West End, Blood Brothers and Crongton Knights.
Music gives a soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination, and life to everything.

Prep Music and Drama
The vibrant Music department in the Prep school allows all students to experience a variety of music from different countries, genres, and periods in history. Their experience in the classroom enables them to play a range of instruments, improvise, compose, sing, and explore music technology using software such as Mixcraft and Cubase. All Prep students are involved in a Choir, including our Key Stage 1 Choir and Key Stage 2 Choir.
All students who play an instrument are strongly encouraged to join our extra-curricular programme. We have a Prep Rock Band, a combined Prep and Senior School Orchestra and Jazz band. The instrumentalists also get opportunities to perform in assemblies, informal tea concerts and more formal evening concerts including the Prep Soiree.
Music and Drama work closely together to produce Christmas Nativities and the annual Summer show, with recent acclaimed performances such as Jungle Book, Rock Bottom and The Lion King.
Prep students can take private music lessons in a wide range of instruments with one of our visiting music teachers. Students in Year 3 and above can take Speech and Drama lessons through LAMDA and have achieved Distinctions across the board over the past few years.

English as an Additional Language
The EAL department is a well-established centre for students whose first language is not English. Individually tailored programmes of study ensure that students can achieve their potential in all subject areas quickly and effectively.
In small groups students gain competence in reading, writing, listening and speaking, allowing them to integrate with ease into school life.
Sixth Formers are prepared for the IELTS examination for entrance into Higher Education. In addition, confidence in spoken English is enhanced by extra-curricular lessons in Oral Communication; this has become so popular that some students are now opting to take Speech and Drama lessons leading to LAMDA examinations.
Students whose English requires improvement before they begin A-level examination courses may join the Foundation Year Sixth Form. Here they will receive intensive English Lessons with the opportunity to join Year 12 classes in their chosen subjects as their English improves. They will then stay at Beechwood to begin their two-year A-level courses, well prepared and ready to achieve to their potential.

Nursery & Preschool
A joyful start to learning, exploration and confidence
Set within 23 acres of beautiful parkland in the heart of Tunbridge Wells, Beechwood’s Nursery and Preschool offers children aged 2 to 4 a nurturing, stimulating environment where curiosity is encouraged and every child is known.
With small groups, caring staff and a rich programme of activities, children build confidence, independence and a love of learning from the very beginning of their school journey.
Beechwood Pre-School is a friendly, caring environment where the teachers cater for individual needs and interests. I have been amazed at how confident and independent my son has become since starting.
Dedicated Spaces for Every Stage
Children thrive when learning is tailored to their age and development. At Beechwood, our Nursery and Preschool are organised into separate year groups, each with their own space, resources and specialist staff.
This ensures every child receives the right balance of care, challenge and encouragement at exactly the right time.
Nursery: Ages 2–3 years
Our youngest children are welcomed into a calm, nurturing and intimate, personalised setting where routines, relationships and communication come first.
Because of our small Nursery groups, each child is truly known by our dedicated staff, who focus on:
Preschool: Ages 3–4 years
In Preschool, children build on these foundations with more structured learning experiences that develop early literacy, numeracy, creativity and social skills.
The term after their third birthday, children are gently assessed against developmental milestones. When ready, they transition into our term-time Preschool, where they benefit from specialist teaching and a richer academic and enrichment programme.
All sessions are delivered by specialist teachers, helping children develop confidence, skills and a love of learning across a wide range of subjects.
By the end of Preschool, children are confident, independent and ready for the transition into Reception.
A Nurturing Environment for children aged 2–4
From their first days with us, children are welcomed into a warm, supportive setting designed around their needs and interests. Our experienced Early Years team focuses on building strong relationships, encouraging communication and developing confidence through purposeful play.
Children learn through exploration, imagination and hands-on experiences, following the Early Years Foundation Stage framework in a way that feels natural, engaging and joyful.
A Seamless Start to School Life
One of the great strengths of Beechwood is the smooth, carefully supported transition from Nursery to Preschool and into Reception.
Children move through each stage of their development in a nurturing and stimulating environment tailored to their individual needs, supported by staff who know them well.
By the time they reach Reception, they are socially confident, independent and ready to thrive.

Forest School
Forest School (England) Network 2002 defines Forest School as: ‘An inspirational process that offers children, young people and adults regular opportunities to achieve, develop confidence and self-esteem through hands-on learning experiences in a local woodland environment.’ Forest School has been actively promoted by practitioners over the last 15 years becoming increasingly popular and we trust that your children will enjoy the experience as much as we do.
Forest School is a unique way for our children to learn in their own environment. It helps to develop confidence, creativity and resilience. It is a learner-centred process carried out outside in all weathers encouraging children to work in teams using their imaginations and natural resources. It promotes holistic development and is suitable for all children of all capabilities.
The sessions support all areas of the child’s learning and development.
Personal, Social and Emotional Development: At Forest School, the children will have the opportunity to play and work alongside their peers. Making relationships by developing friendly behaviour, initiating conversations and working in teams. They will also learn how to manage their own behaviour by following instructions, abiding by the rules, and adapting their behaviour to new environments.
Communication and Language: Forest School promotes communication by allowing children to listen to each other during team activities. Following directions and responding to simple instructions. Gives children the opportunity to question why things happen and give explanations.
Physical Development: Forest School allows children to move freely developing their gross motor skills by climbing and jumping. Using tools develops their fine motor skills.
Literacy: Forest School allows children to reflect or listen to a stories in small groups at the end of the session. It also gives them the opportunity to give mean to the marks they make.
Mathematics: Forest School gives the children lots of opportunity to develop their maths skills, counting object, grouping and recognising shapes in the environment.
Understanding the World: Forest School gives them the opportunity to talk about things they have observed such as plants, animals and natural objects. They are also able to build camps and dens using natural resources.
Expressive Arts and Design: Forest School gives children the opportunity to engage in imaginative play and use natural resources as props to support role play. These are jus a few examples of the opportunities for learning Forest School Leaders will be able to introduce to your child to promote their development in all areas.
Forest School Testimonials
From the moment my daughter started Forest School, her enthusiasm for learning has soared to new heights. The transformation has been remarkable. Seeing her come home excitedly talking about her adventures in the forest and the new discoveries she's made is so heartwarming.
What I love most about the Forest School program is its hands-on approach to education. Instead of being confined to a classroom, my child is out in the fresh air, exploring the natural world around him. It's incredible to see his curiosity sparked and his imagination ignited as he engages with the environment in meaningful ways.

Nursery & Preschool
A joyful start to learning, exploration and confidence
Set within 23 acres of beautiful parkland in the heart of Tunbridge Wells, Beechwood’s Nursery and Preschool offers children aged 2 to 4 a nurturing, stimulating environment where curiosity is encouraged and every child is known.
With small groups, caring staff and a rich programme of activities, children build confidence, independence and a love of learning from the very beginning of their school journey.
Beechwood Pre-School is a friendly, caring environment where the teachers cater for individual needs and interests. I have been amazed at how confident and independent my son has become since starting.
Dedicated Spaces for Every Stage
Children thrive when learning is tailored to their age and development. At Beechwood, our Nursery and Preschool are organised into separate year groups, each with their own space, resources and specialist staff.
This ensures every child receives the right balance of care, challenge and encouragement at exactly the right time.
Nursery: Ages 2–3 years
Our youngest children are welcomed into a calm, nurturing and intimate, personalised setting where routines, relationships and communication come first.
Because of our small Nursery groups, each child is truly known by our dedicated staff, who focus on:
Preschool: Ages 3–4 years
In Preschool, children build on these foundations with more structured learning experiences that develop early literacy, numeracy, creativity and social skills.
The term after their third birthday, children are gently assessed against developmental milestones. When ready, they transition into our term-time Preschool, where they benefit from specialist teaching and a richer academic and enrichment programme.
All sessions are delivered by specialist teachers, helping children develop confidence, skills and a love of learning across a wide range of subjects.
By the end of Preschool, children are confident, independent and ready for the transition into Reception.
A Nurturing Environment for children aged 2–4
From their first days with us, children are welcomed into a warm, supportive setting designed around their needs and interests. Our experienced Early Years team focuses on building strong relationships, encouraging communication and developing confidence through purposeful play.
Children learn through exploration, imagination and hands-on experiences, following the Early Years Foundation Stage framework in a way that feels natural, engaging and joyful.
A Seamless Start to School Life
One of the great strengths of Beechwood is the smooth, carefully supported transition from Nursery to Preschool and into Reception.
Children move through each stage of their development in a nurturing and stimulating environment tailored to their individual needs, supported by staff who know them well.
By the time they reach Reception, they are socially confident, independent and ready to thrive.

A Day In The Life
Children not booked into breakfast club from 7.30am can be dropped off from 8.00am in the Pre-School. As their friends arrive, they play freely until registration at 8.30am when our session begins.
Each day is timetabled and while much of the day is in the setting or grounds surrounding it, the children have structured lessons in Cookery, PE, Music and Forest School with specialist teachers during the week.
Depending on the daily timetable a snack is scheduled from around 10.00am – 10.30am where the children are offered a selection of fruit, vegetables, cheese, crackers, and occasional treats from our kitchen. We also provide milk and water.
Our children have access to free flow throughout their sessions to enjoy time both indoors and outside in our designated play area.
At 12.00pm the children eat lunch in our refectory seated with their teachers to promote good table manners and to ensure the children eat well.
At 1.00pm our morning session finishes and those children going home are collected from the Pre-School. The remaining children enjoy playtime with the Reception class until 1.30pm.
During the afternoon the children enjoy a range of activities, child initiated, and adult led. At 3.00pm the children have the opportunity to make their own sandwiches for an afternoon snack.
Our session finishes at 3.30pm however collection is up until 4.00pm when wrap around care can be provided until 6.00pm if required.

Request a Prospectus
To register your interest and to receive a prospectus, please fill in the form below and a member of our Admissions team will be in touch shortly. Please note that fields marked with an asterisk (*) must be completed before clicking submit.
Data Protection In accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), we hereby wish to notify you of how we intend to use the information you are providing on this form.
The data you have provided will be stored by Beechwood School (the School) for the purposes of communicating with you as you progress through our admissions process. The data we have requested is justified as the first stage in progressing your potential application and as a legitimate interest. Your data will be kept indefinitely or until such a time as you ask for it to be deleted. Your data will not be shared with anyone outside of the School except for the processing of your potential application. Communication may include letters, emails, telephone calls and newsletters. If you believe we have misused your data, you have the right to complain to the ICO.

Senior Academic
Beechwood continues to out-perform the GCSE national average. We are incredibly proud of all of our students’ achievements and wish them continued success with their future studies.
We follow a broad curriculum to provide a balance that can stimulate the talents of every student. During Year 9, students will have the opportunity to learn about our wide range of GCSE subjects and make their option choices.
Class sizes vary from about 8 – 20, according to the subject options taken. Mathematics and English are taught in ability groups.
We offer over 16 option choices for GCSE on top of the core subjects.
To find out more about our GCSE provision, please click here.
Our dedicated team includes trained teachers, specialising in areas such as Dyslexia, Maths, and Speech and Language. Students needing support are identified when they enter Beechwood, through screening, or referral by teachers, and an individual programme is put in place. This may include individual lessons or Directed Study and may involve replacing a curriculum subject with time spent in Learning Development. The subject to be replaced is considered on an individual basis, so that we can give the students the best curriculum programme to suit their needs.
Students are screened for extra time and other access arrangements in external examinations. This can include in-school assessment or referral to other professionals such as an Educational Psychologist.
We work closely with subject teachers, and the Learning Enhancement Hub to improve students’ learning experience and skills. All students are base-line assessed at the beginning of the school year and these results are used to form reading and spelling booster groups before school and at lunchtimes if necessary. Other support groups are put in place depending on need.

Class sizes vary from about 8 – 20, according to the subject options taken. Mathematics continues to be taught in ability groups.
The Performing Arts of Music and Drama are an important part of life at Beechwood. More than half the students have extra lessons in singing or instrumental music and opportunities to perform are wide and varied. Students of all ages and abilities are encouraged to take part in a variety of dramatic activities and Theatre Studies is a popular and successful choice for many students both at GCSE and A-level.

Key Stage 3
We follow a broad curriculum in order to provide a balance that can stimulate the talents of every student.
The core subjects of English, Mathematics and Science are taught throughout Years 7-11, together with Religious Education, Physical Education and Personal, Social, Citizenship and Health Education (PSCHE), which are compulsory for all year groups. Further details may be found in the Years 7-9 Curriculum Handbook which is available below.
Class sizes are small, with up to 20 students. Most groups are mixed ability, with some subjects, such as Mathematics, set by ability where it is educationally advantageous.
Year 7 students take French and German or Spanish. International students who require additional English support will have EAL lessons instead of one or both European languages. The Design Technology programme includes product design, textiles, and food technology for both boys and girls.
In Year 8 there is the opportunity to develop research and analytical skills by taking the Junior EPQ programme.
These essential skills for life will benefit Beechwood students while they are at university and also as they begin their careers
